claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically contains residual porosity and micro-defects.
Carbon or B4C can serve as a low-melting-point, transient-liquid-forming sintering additive for ZrB2.
A minor concentration of carbon or B4C will permit ZrB2 sintering at 2000–2100 °C rather than at or above 2300 °C.
An inert or reducing sintering atmosphere will control oxidation during lower-temperature processing.
An optimized low additive concentration can produce temporary liquid formation without leaving a permanent secondary phase.
The additive will generate a transient liquid phase at ZrB2 particle contacts.
The transient liquid phase will promote particle rearrangement and mass transport.
Promoted particle rearrangement and mass transport will enhance densification and decrease porosity.
The additive locally lowers the melting point during ZrB2 sintering.
Temporary liquid formation improves particle packing and diffusion.
Improved densification reduces the number and size of residual holes and defects.
Residual holes and defects can evolve into critical flaws during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure and cause component failure.
Lower-temperature additive-doped ZrB2 will have similar or improved mechanical strength relative to conventionally prepared ZrB2.
Lower-temperature additive-doped ZrB2 will retain greater structural integrity during long-term liquid plating exposure.
Lower-temperature additive-doped ZrB2 will have markedly lower porosity and fewer initiation sites for liquid-induced degradation.
The proposed intervention is expected to work within an approximately 2000–2100 °C sintering window and at low additive concentrations.
The benefits may not occur at substantially different sintering temperatures or additive concentrations.
Transient liquid-phase mechanisms in other material systems suggest improved densification.
The effects of the intervention on ZrB2 phase stability, mechanical properties, and long-term plating-bath corrosion resistance have not been quantitatively established.
